cards.text: Solomon is king of Israel now, anointed in his father David's place. Hiram, king of Tyre, hears the news and sends envoys to Solomon. Friend, the man barely has the crown on and somebody's already knocking.

cards.question: Hiram, king of Tyre, sends envoys to Solomon because he and David had always been enemies. True or false?

cards.text: Solomon sends a message back to Hiram, and friend, this is NOT a thank-you note. It's about a house for the Name of the LORD, the one his father David never got to build.

cards.question: Solomon says David couldn't build the house because of the ___ he faced on all sides.

cards.text: But now the LORD has given Solomon rest on every side, with no adversary and no crisis. Friend, I live alone on a cookie planet and I STILL can't get one week with no crisis.

cards.question: Solomon says his plan goes back to something the LORD told his father David. What did the LORD say about building the house?

cards.text: So here's the ask: cut down cedars of Lebanon, with Solomon's servants working right beside Hiram's. And Solomon will pay WHATEVER wages Hiram sets, which, friend, is a blank check.

cards.question: Solomon wants the Sidonians, Hiram's people, on the cedar job. Why?

answers.text: Nobody in Israel logs like them
Hiram owes David a very big favor
Israel's men are all away at war

cards.text: Hiram reads Solomon's message and rejoices greatly. Friend, when I get a message, I stare at it for ten minutes and then type back "ok."

cards.question: Reading Solomon's message, Hiram says, "Blessed be the LORD this day!" and praises Him for giving David a wise son. True or false?

cards.text: Hiram writes back: he'll do all Solomon desires about the cedar and cypress timber. His servants will haul the logs from Lebanon down to the Sea.

cards.question: Hiram's servants have the logs at the Sea. How will Hiram get them to the place Solomon picks?

answers.text: Float them as rafts by sea

cards.text: When the rafts arrive, Hiram will separate the logs, and Solomon's people can take them away. Friend, that's a delivery guy who unpacks the boxes for you, and NOBODY has ever treated me that well.

cards.question: And in exchange for all that timber? Hiram says Solomon can meet his needs by providing his ___ with ___.

cards.text: So Hiram provides all the cedar and cypress Solomon wants, and Solomon sends 20,000 cors of wheat and 20,000 baths of pure olive oil for Hiram's household. Friend, I used to think a double batch was a big order.

cards.question: Solomon sends Hiram the wheat and olive oil just once, as a one-time payment. True or false?

cards.text: Then the text tells us the LORD gave Solomon wisdom. Friend, the LORD gave ME a mustache that packs cookie boxes, so we BOTH got blessed, but I'm pretty sure his gift wins.

cards.question: The LORD gives Solomon wisdom even though He had never promised it. True or false?
The text sums up how things stand between Hiram and Solomon. What does it say?

answers.text: There was peace and they made a treaty
They stayed friendly but signed nothing
They argued over the price of timber

cards.text: Now Solomon needs hands. He conscripts a labor force of 30,000 men from all Israel and sends them to Lebanon in monthly shifts of 10,000.

cards.question: A worker in Solomon's 30,000-man labor force does his month in Lebanon. How long is he home before his next shift?

cards.text: Adoniram is in charge of the forced labor, and in the mountains Solomon has 70,000 porters, 80,000 stonecutters and 3,300 foremen supervising the workers. Friend, I run this whole bakery with ZERO foremen, and it SHOWS.
Then the king gives an order for the temple's foundation. Remember those 80,000 stonecutters? They're about to earn their keep.

cards.question: Solomon gives an order for the temple's foundation. What does he want it laid with?
Solomon's builders quarry the stone and prepare the timber all on their own, with no help from outside Israel. True or false?

cards.text: Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders and the Gebalites, men from the city of Gebal, get the timber and stone ready for the temple. Friend, the dough's mixed and resting on the counter, and this story is still waiting on the oven.

findings.problem: The earlier cards give no basis for choosing "household" and "food." Completing the sentence with "army" and food, or "household" and gold, would also be plausible, so the baker must guess details they have not seen rather than reason out the meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "They stayed friendly but signed nothing" is not clearly false. First Kings 5:12 says Hiram and Solomon made a treaty, but it does not say whether anything was written or signed, so a baker could argue that this option is compatible with the right answer.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
